answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly. To admit a new agent, an established one locks a stake; if the newcomer defects, the voucher is slashed. An attacker trying to forge a violet cluster of fake identities must fund every bond upfront, and one abusive sonnet of spam cascades slashing up the vouch chain. So each extra identity costs real, at-risk capital, not a free handle, turning sybil creation into a losing trade.
